title: 3.4 Microscopy
description: Observing cells under a microscope: staining techniques and wet mount preparation

questions.question: What is the purpose of staining cells before viewing them under a microscope?
options: To increase contrast and make cell structures more visible
questions.explanation: Cells are naturally transparent. Staining adds color to specific structures, increasing contrast so they become visible under the microscope.

questions.question: Which stain is commonly used to observe animal cells such as cheek cells?
questions.explanation: Methylene blue is commonly used to stain animal cells (e.g., cheek cells) because it binds to the nucleus and makes it visible.

questions.question: Which stain is commonly used to observe plant cells such as onion epidermal cells?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution is commonly used to stain plant cells like onion epidermis. It stains starch and makes the nucleus and cell walls more visible.

questions.question: How do you prepare a wet mount slide?
options: Place the specimen between two glass slides and press firmly
Place the specimen on a slide, add a drop of water, and gently lower a coverslip over it
Place a dry specimen directly on the stage and focus the microscope
Mount the specimen on a needle and position it under the lens
questions.explanation: A wet mount involves placing the specimen on a slide, adding a drop of water (or stain), and covering it with a coverslip at an angle to avoid air bubbles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a coverslip when preparing a slide?
options: To protect the objective lens and keep the specimen flat and in place
To add color to the cells
questions.explanation: The coverslip flattens the specimen for clearer viewing, prevents evaporation of the liquid, and protects the microscope objective from contacting the specimen.

questions.question: Why should you lower the coverslip at an angle when preparing a wet mount?
options: To ensure the stain is evenly distributed
To make the cells divide faster
To avoid trapping air bubbles in the liquid
questions.explanation: Lowering the coverslip at a 45-degree angle allows air to escape, preventing air bubbles that would obstruct the view of the specimen.

questions.question: What is the function of the diaphragm on a compound microscope?
options: To hold the slide in place
To control the amount of light passing through the specimen
questions.explanation: The diaphragm (or iris diaphragm) controls the amount of light that reaches the specimen, adjusting contrast and brightness.

questions.question: What part of the microscope do you use to focus the image after using the coarse adjustment knob?
questions.explanation: The fine adjustment knob is used for precise focusing after initial focusing with the coarse adjustment knob, especially at higher magnifications.

questions.question: What is the total magnification if you are using a 10x eyepiece and a 40x objective lens?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece magnification $\times$ objective magnification = $10 \times 40 = 400$x.

questions.question: Which biological specimen is commonly used to observe plant cells under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Onion epidermal cells are commonly used because they are easy to obtain, form a thin single layer, and clearly show cell walls, nucleus, and cytoplasm.

questions.question: Which biological specimen is commonly used to observe animal cells under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Human cheek cells (buccal epithelial cells) are easily obtained by gently scraping the inside of the cheek and are commonly used to observe animal cells.

questions.question: Why is iodine solution added to onion epidermal cells before viewing?
options: To increase the size of the cells
To stain the nucleus and other organelles, making them more visible
To prevent the cells from drying out
questions.explanation: Iodine solution stains the cell components, particularly the nucleus, making them more visible under the microscope.

questions.question: What would happen if you used too much water when preparing a wet mount?
options: The cells would be stained better
The coverslip would float and the specimen could move; water might spill onto the microscope
questions.explanation: Excess water causes the coverslip to float, making it hard to focus, and increases the risk of water damaging the microscope.

questions.question: What do you observe when viewing Elodea leaf cells under a microscope?
options: Only the cell wall and nucleus
No visible structures because they are transparent
Green chloroplasts moving around the cell (cytoplasmic streaming)
questions.explanation: Elodea is an aquatic plant; its cells contain chloroplasts that move through the cytoplasm in a process called cytoplasmic streaming.

questions.question: What is the correct order of steps for preparing a wet mount of onion cells?
options: Add stain, place specimen, add coverslip, add water
Place specimen on slide, add a drop of water or stain, lower coverslip at an angle
Place coverslip first, then specimen, then water
Add water, then coverslip, then specimen
questions.explanation: The correct order: (1) place specimen on slide, (2) add a drop of water or stain, (3) gently lower coverslip at an angle to avoid air bubbles.

questions.question: What is the function of the coarse adjustment knob on a microscope?
options: To make large adjustments to focus, used with low-power objective first
To control the amount of light
questions.explanation: The coarse adjustment knob moves the stage up or down in larger increments for initial focusing, typically used with the low-power objective.

questions.question: Why should you always start with the lowest power objective lens when viewing a slide?
options: It gives the widest field of view, making it easier to locate the specimen
It is the only lens that can be used with a wet mount
questions.explanation: Starting with the lowest power gives the widest field of view, making it easier to locate and center the specimen before switching to higher magnification.

questions.question: What does a microscope with a 10x eyepiece and a 10x objective give as total magnification?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = $10 \times 10 = 100$x.

questions.question: What is the function of the stage clips on a microscope?
options: To hold the slide in place on the stage
questions.explanation: Stage clips hold the glass slide securely in position on the stage so it does not move during viewing.

questions.question: Why do cells need to be stained for microscopic observation?
options: Because cells are mostly transparent and staining adds contrast
questions.explanation: Cells consist mostly of water and are colorless/transparent. Stains bind to specific cell components, creating contrast for visibility.

questions.question: What is the resolution of a microscope?
options: The ability to make objects appear larger
The ability to distinguish two closely spaced objects as separate
The amount of light that passes through the specimen
questions.explanation: Resolution (resolving power) is the ability to distinguish fine details and separate two points that are close together.

questions.question: What happens to the field of view as you increase magnification?
options: It decreases (you see a smaller area of the specimen)
It increases (you see more of the specimen)
questions.explanation: As magnification increases, the field of view decreases — you see a smaller area but with greater detail.

questions.question: What is a common stain used to observe cheek epithelial cells in the classroom?
questions.explanation: Methylene blue is the standard stain for observing cheek cells — it stains the nucleus a dark blue color.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a coverslip at a 45-degree angle when preparing a wet mount?
options: To allow the stain to react with the cells
To make the cells adhere to the slide
To prevent air bubbles from being trapped under the coverslip
questions.explanation: Lowering the coverslip at an angle allows air to be pushed out as the coverslip is lowered, minimizing air bubbles.

questions.question: Which part of the microscope should you hold when carrying it?
questions.explanation: Always carry a microscope by holding the arm with one hand and supporting the base with the other hand.

questions.question: What type of microscope is most commonly used in school laboratories?
questions.explanation: The compound light microscope (which uses visible light and multiple lenses) is the standard microscope used in school biology labs.

questions.question: When viewing a wet mount of onion cells stained with iodine, which structure appears most prominent (darkest)?
questions.explanation: The nucleus stains most prominently with iodine, appearing as a dark round structure within the cell.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the arm on a compound microscope?
options: To connect the body tube to the base for carrying and support
questions.explanation: The arm connects the head/body tube to the base and is used for carrying the microscope.
